title: Goal-Aware Identification and Rectification of Misinformation in Multi-Agent Systems
claim: Injected misleading information spreads through agent networks and causes task failure; a goal-aware defense localizes and rectifies it to restore success.
layout: Taxonomy banner top-left, injection panel bottom-left, defense panel right, arrow flow
description: A slanted multi-panel figure. Top-left has two pink banners classifying injected content. Malicious-information is semantically harmful and offensive, shown with a radiation icon, a warning triangle and a devil face. Mis-information is semantically harmless and misleading, shown with a bomb icon, a green mask and a dizzy face. Bottom-left is a blue panel titled Misinformation Injection. It shows a network of robot icons linked by pink arrows, with a red devil at the centre and a red injector robot. Several robots carry 'Misled!' bubbles, and a red 'Task Failed!' arrow points out. A blue striped arrow leads right to the yellow ARGUS panel. That panel has the same robot network with a shield and magnifier icons for Adaptive Localization. Curved arrows lead up to a second network with green edges, blue shields and 'Task Success!'. Badges read Multi-Round and Training-Free.
caption: Classification of Information Injection Techniques in MAS by injected content type, alongside corresponding defense frameworks.
abstract: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (MASs) have demonstrated strong advantages in addressing complex real-world tasks. However, due to the introduction of additional attack surfaces, MASs are particularly vulnerable to misinformation injection. To facilitate a deeper understanding of misinformation propagation dynamics within these systems, we introduce MisinfoTask, a novel dataset featuring complex, realistic tasks designed to evaluate MAS robustness against such threats. Building upon this, we propose ARGUS, a two-stage, training-free defense framework leveraging goal-aware reasoning for precise misinformation rectification within information flows. Our experiments demonstrate that in challenging misinformation scenarios, ARGUS exhibits significant efficacy across various injection attacks, achieving an average reduction in misinformation toxicity of approximately 28.17% and improving task success rates under attack by approximately 10.33%. Our code and dataset is available at: https://github.com/zhrli324/ARGUS.
